title: Ramayana Trailer Postponed as Sony Pictures Signs On for Global Distribution
excerpt: Producer Namit Malhotra delays the public trailer launch to coordinate a worldwide rollout after Sony Pictures Entertainment boards the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer as its international distributor.
body:
• The Ramayana trailer, originally set for public release on July 24, has been postponed to coordinate with new global distributor Sony Pictures Entertainment.
  • Producer Namit Malhotra called the partnership a first in over 100 years of Indian cinema — the film will be released globally like a major Hollywood production.
  • The film stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi and Sunny Deol, directed by Nitesh Tiwari.
  • The trailer had been previewed at San Diego Comic-Con just hours before the postponement was announced.

A Four-Minute Trailer the World Almost Saw

Hours before the Ramayana trailer was to go live on Friday morning, producer Namit Malhotra pulled the plug. The four-minute trailer had already been shown to select media and fans at a grand unveiling in Delhi last week and previewed again at a San Diego Comic-Con panel on Thursday — where stars Ranbir Kapoor and Yash joined director Nitesh Tiwari for a discussion. But the public digital release, scheduled for 8 AM on July 24, was shelved at the last minute.

The reason: Sony Pictures Entertainment has signed on as the film's international distributor outside India. Malhotra said the partnership required a globally coordinated trailer launch rather than an India-first rollout.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=oNxG3Z-vvcU

'A Moment of Great Pride'

"Today is a very special moment for our Ramayana," Malhotra wrote in a note posted to Instagram late Thursday. "My dream of taking Ramayana to the world is now a reality with our partnership with Sony Pictures Entertainment. In over 100+ years of Indian Cinema, this will become a moment of great pride where Ramayana will be shown to the entire world like any major global Hollywood film."

https://x.com/PeopleOfTheInt/status/2080739795580461282

"This is special as it opens the door for people of the world to discover the richness of our culture and our stories with renewed pride and enthusiasm."

— Namit Malhotra, Producer, Prime Focus Studios

A Potential Spider-Man Pairing

Fan speculation has centered on whether the Ramayana trailer could be attached to the theatrical release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Sony's upcoming tentpole starring Tom Holland. The film is projected to open with ₹50-60 crore in India and between $550-700 million worldwide, making it one of the largest marketing platforms available. No official confirmation has been made.

What the Deal Means for Indian Cinema

The Sony partnership represents a significant escalation in international ambitions for Indian-made films. Ramayana, envisioned as a global cinematic spectacle, will release in multiple languages including a premium English-language version. The film is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, whose Dangal remains one of India's highest-grossing films globally.

For the Indian diaspora, the deal means Ramayana could see the kind of wide international release typically reserved for Hollywood productions — playing in mainstream multiplexes rather than limited South Asian-focused screens.
